_meta.note: Pokemon GO search-bar vocabulary. This file is what the linter validates against. It REPLACES the guesswork in pogofiltersConfig.js's old hardcoded GAME_KEYWORDS set, which came from PogoFilters/pokemon_go_search_filters.md - a document whose own header says 'File offered from Gemini.ai / May need verification for 2026 filters'. That unverified list is why the linter wrongly flagged mega1/mega2/mega3 as unknown.

confidence.confirmed: documented by two or more independent sources that agree
confidence.single-source: only one source documents it - probably real, treat a lint warning here as soft
confidence.disputed: sources disagree on spelling or existence - the linter must NOT flag these as errors
confidence.in-use: no source documents it, but it appears in Trey's live filters and has been working. Accepted, never flagged - real usage outranks a third-party cheat sheet.

couldNotFetch: https://niantic.helpshift.com/hc/en/6-pokemon-go/faq/1486-searching-filtering-your-pokemon-inventory/ (403 to scripted fetch - the official page is the only real authority and could not be read)
_meta.verificationRule: Nothing here outranks an in-game test. When a term is confirmed or disproved in game, record it in PogoFilters/FilterRules.md with a date and change its confidence here.

or.note: Comma is confirmed by every source. Semicolon and colon are claimed by pogocleanup and pokexperience; pipe only by Dexerto and is likely wrong. Only ',' should be relied on.

family.meaning: prefix a species name to include its whole evolution line, e.g. +bulbasaur

tag.meaning: search a custom tag, e.g. #battle. Bare '#' matches any tagged Pokemon; '!#' matches untagged.
tag.important: This is the documented syntax for TAGS. Trey's own 'Megas unlabled' filter uses !#Mega, so the prefix form is in real use. Whether a BARE tag name (e.g. !Pvp) also matches a tag, or only matches species names, is NOT documented by any source and needs an in-game test - it affects almost every filter in Existingfilters.md.

nickname.meaning: quoted string matches a custom nickname

keywords.note: Documented as ONE word by every source.

Not in any cheat sheet, but Trey's live filters use the spaced form and have been in service a long time. Real usage outranks a third-party doc's spelling, so this is accepted rather than flagged. Confirm in game and record the answer in FilterRules.md.
Plural spaced form, used throughout Existingfilters.md. See the note on 'ultra beast'.
pokexperience says 'genderless', pogocleanup says 'genderunknown'. Neither is confirmed.

keywords.meaning: evolving registers a new dex entry
needs a special item to evolve

keywords.note: Any casing of xxl captures ONLY XXL, never XXS - confirmed in game, see FilterRules.md rule 3.

patterns.meaning: mega0 = can mega but never has; mega1 = Base Level; mega2 = High Level; mega3 = Max Level. Range form mega1-3 also works.
patterns.note: THESE ARE REAL. The old hardcoded keyword list did not contain them, which is why the linter wrongly flagged them.

patterns.meaning: cp1500 exact; cp1500- is 1500 and above; cp-1500 is 1500 and below; cp10-100 is a range.

patterns.note: Trey deliberately uses the reversed form year2020-2015 for mass-deletion filters. Do not 'fix' it - see FilterRules.md rule 6.

patterns.meaning: Individual IV values are NUMBER FIRST, e.g. 15attack. There is no 'stamina' term - the stamina IV is searched as hp.
patterns.note: The old config listed attack/defense/stamina as PREFIX operators (attack15). Both sources document the opposite order, and no source mentions 'stamina' at all.

patterns.meaning: @move any slot; @1 fast; @2 charged; @3 second charged. @special = legacy/exclusive, @weather = weather boosted.

patterns.note: Overlaps dexNumber - a token like #150 is ambiguous between a dex number and a tag literally named 150. The linter treats a digits-only #token as a dex number.

knownUnknowns: Whether a BARE tag name (Pvp) matches a tag, or whether the # prefix is required. Affects nearly every filter in Existingfilters.md.
Whether 'ultra beasts' (spaced, plural) works as well as the documented 'ultrabeast'.
Whether ';' and ':' really work as OR alongside ','.
Whether there is any upper bound on filter length - nothing was hit at 913 characters.
